assessment: This fundamental study generated a single-cell atlas of mouse periosteal cells under both steady-state and fracture healing conditions to address the knowledge gap regarding cellular composition of the periosteum and their responses to injury. Based on convincing transcriptome analyses and experimental validation, the authors identified the injury induced fibrogenic cell (IIFC) as a characteristic cell type appearing in the bone regeneration process and proposed that the IIFC is a progenitor undergoing osteochondrogenic differentiation. This study will provide a significant publicly accessible dataset to reexamine the expression of the reported periosteal stem and progenitor cell markers.
